headline.purpose: Page and section titles (h1-h4). Weight and tracking carry the hierarchy, not a bespoke size scale.

reading.purpose: Prose the doctor actually reads: call summaries, transcripts, agent replies.

micro.purpose: Dense metadata: timestamps, chips, table furniture.

shadows.name: soft
shadows.purpose: Resting elevation: cards, the active nav pill, the mic button at rest.

shadows.name: float
shadows.purpose: Genuinely detached elements: the patient peek popover, the active mic button.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: Default easing for slides, presses, and the mode-switch thumb.

motion.name: pulse-ring
motion.purpose: Status dot for a call in progress.

motion.name: mic-ring
motion.purpose: Two offset rings breathing outward from the mic button while listening or speaking.

motion.name: eq-bar
motion.purpose: Three-bar equaliser while Medley is speaking.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The default call-to-action: ink fill, near-white text.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; height: 36px; padding: 0 16px; border-radius: 8px; background: oklch(0.21 0 0); color: oklch(0.99 0 0); font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; border: none; cursor: pointer; transition: opacity 150ms ease-out, transform 120ms cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { opacity: 0.9; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid oklch(0.21 0 0); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: scale(0.985); }

components.name: Outline Button
components.description: Secondary action: hairline border, transparent fill.
components.css: .ds-btn-outline { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; height: 36px; padding: 0 16px; border-radius: 8px; background: transparent; color: oklch(0.21 0 0); border: 1px solid oklch(0.68 0 0); font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 150ms ease-out; } .ds-btn-outline:hover { background: oklch(0.955 0 0); } .ds-btn-outline:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid oklch(0.21 0 0); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Input Field
components.description: Text field with the field-only border, kept darker than a row divider so it reads as a control.
components.html: <input class="ds-input" placeholder="Ring John tomorrow about the new tablets" />
components.css: .ds-input { height: 36px; width: 100%; padding: 0 12px; border-radius: 8px; border: 1px solid oklch(0.68 0 0); background: transparent; color: oklch(0.21 0 0); font-size: 0.9375rem; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: oklch(0.47 0 0); } .ds-input:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid oklch(0.21 0 0); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Status Badge
components.description: Mood/status pill. Colour maps to one of the four named clinical states; neutral gets no colour at all.
components.css: .ds-badge { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; border-radius: 6px; padding: 4px 10px; font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 500; } .ds-badge--neutral { background: oklch(0.955 0 0); color: oklch(0.47 0 0); } .ds-badge--flag { background: oklch(0.96 0.03 18); color: oklch(0.48 0.19 18); } .ds-badge--overdue { background: oklch(0.96 0.035 75); color: oklch(0.52 0.13 65); } .ds-badge--done { background: oklch(0.95 0.03 155); color: oklch(0.46 0.10 155); }

components.name: Card
components.description: The base elevated surface: a distinct plane above canvas via background alone, no shadow at rest.
components.css: .ds-card { background: oklch(1 0 0); color: oklch(0.21 0 0); border: 1px solid oklch(0.915 0 0); border-radius: 14px; padding: 24px; } .ds-card__title { font-weight: 600; font-size: 1.125rem; line-height: 1.2; } .ds-card__meta { margin-top: 4px; font-size: 0.875rem; color: oklch(0.47 0 0); }

components.name: Mode Switch
components.description: Signature control: a two-option pill radiogroup with one sliding thumb, used to choose voice vs. text conversation.
components.css: .ds-modeswitch { position: relative; display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr; width: 280px; border-radius: 9999px; border: 1px solid oklch(0.915 0 0); background: oklch(0.955 0 0); padding: 4px; } .ds-modeswitch__thumb { position: absolute; inset: 4px auto 4px 4px; width: calc(50% - 4px); border-radius: 9999px; background: oklch(1 0 0); box-shadow: 0 1px 2px oklch(0 0 0 / 0.04), 0 2px 8px oklch(0 0 0 / 0.04); transition: transform 200ms cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1); } .ds-modeswitch__opt { position: relative; z-index: 1; height: 44px; border: none; background: transparent; border-radius: 9999px; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; color: oklch(0.47 0 0); cursor: pointer; } .ds-modeswitch__opt--active { color: oklch(0.21 0 0); }

components.name: Voice Console Mic
components.description: Signature control: the large circular mic button, resting state shown; active state fills ink and adds two breathing rings (see motion.mic-ring).
components.html: <button class="ds-mic" aria-label="Start talking to Medley"><svg width="28" height="28" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="M12 1a3 3 0 0 0-3 3v8a3 3 0 0 0 6 0V4a3 3 0 0 0-3-3z"></path><path d="M19 10v2a7 7 0 0 1-14 0v-2"></path><line x1="12" y1="19" x2="12" y2="23"></line><line x1="8" y1="23" x2="16" y2="23"></line></svg></button>
components.css: .ds-mic { display: grid; place-items: center; width: 80px; height: 80px; border-radius: 9999px; background: oklch(1 0 0); color: oklch(0.21 0 0); border: 1px solid oklch(0.68 0 0); box-shadow: 0 1px 2px oklch(0 0 0 / 0.04), 0 2px 8px oklch(0 0 0 / 0.04); cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 200ms, box-shadow 200ms; } .ds-mic:hover { background: oklch(0.955 0 0); border-color: oklch(0.21 0 0 / 0.3); } .ds-mic:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid oklch(0.21 0 0); outline-offset: 4px; }

narrative.overview:
Medley reads like a piece of clinical instrumentation, not a SaaS dashboard wearing a healthcare skin. The canvas is a true neutral at chroma 0 — no warm cream tint, because a paper-toned near-white is the saturated AI default and reads as generated the moment a second person has seen a few. Nothing is coloured for decoration. Primary actions are ink-filled, not branded; surfaces are grey-on-grey, distinguished by two planes (a sidebar rail one shade off the content) rather than by hue.

Colour is a clinical signal, not a mood. Exactly four things in the entire product carry saturated colour — a call happening right now, a follow-up gone overdue, a safeguarding or low-mood flag, a completed call — and nothing else is allowed to borrow those hues. A doctor reading the screen from a metre away between patients can tell what needs attention without hunting, and a quiet overdue case is exactly as visually loud as an urgent one, because loudness was never the mechanism.

Warmth is deliberate but structural, not material: it lives in the copy voice and in small physical details — a pressed-state scale on every tappable control, a mic button that breathes with two offset rings while listening, an equaliser that dances while Medley speaks. A display serif was tried on patient names and rejected: it read as warmth in a mock-up and as inconsistency in a tool opened forty times a day. One family, many weights, does the whole job.
keyCharacteristics: True neutral (chroma 0) canvas and ink — no warm or cool tint anywhere except the four state colours
Exactly four saturated hues in the whole system, each meaning one clinical state, never decorative
Single sans family (Geist) at multiple weights instead of a display/body pairing
Two-plane structure: a recessed sidebar rail against a lighter content plane
Named, motion-driven state: pulsing dots, breathing mic rings, an equaliser — always paired with a written status word, never colour or motion alone
Every animated cue has a static reduced-motion equivalent that still communicates the same state

rules.name: The Four Signals Rule
rules.body: Saturated colour exists nowhere except Live Ember, Overdue Amber, Flag Crimson, and Done Moss. If a new state needs colour, it either maps onto one of these four or the system has grown a fifth meaning — treat that as a real design decision, not a quick addition.

rules.name: The Colour-Is-Never-Alone Rule
rules.body: Every colour-coded state also carries a written word or an accessible label. A status dot next to its own label is decorative; a status dot standing alone announces itself as an image with a name.

rules.name: The One-Family Rule
rules.body: No second typeface, ever, at any weight. Hierarchy is weight + size + spacing, because a label opened forty times a day should not also carry a font decision.

rules.name: Tabular Numerals Rule
rules.body: Anything that updates in place — call durations, timestamps, live readings — uses tabular-nums so digits don't jitter sideways as they change.

rules.name: The Two-Plane Rule
rules.body: Depth communicates structure (rail vs. content, resting vs. floating), never brand or decoration. A third shadow tier is a sign a component needs restructuring, not a bigger shadow.

dos: Do keep colour to the four named states (Live Ember, Overdue Amber, Flag Crimson, Done Moss). Anything else stays neutral.
Do pair every colour cue with a written word or accessible label — colour is never the sole carrier of state.
Do use the named z-index scale (--z-rail … --z-palette) for any new overlay instead of an arbitrary value.
Do give every animated state cue (pulses, rings, equalisers) a static prefers-reduced-motion equivalent that still communicates the change.
Do keep the input-field border (~3:1) visibly darker than the row-divider border (~1.23:1) — they answer different questions.
donts: Don't introduce a second typeface, including a display serif. It was tried on patient names and rejected as inconsistent in a tool opened forty times a day.
Don't tint the canvas or card surfaces warm (cream, paper-tone). The neutral is chroma-0 on purpose.
Don't give the 'neutral' mood, 'declined' status, or 'queued' status any colour beyond the quiet grey.
Don't add a new shadow tier beyond Soft and Float. If something needs a third level of depth, restructure the plane instead.
Don't style focus rings per component. One :focus-visible rule at the base layer covers everything.
